newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar stages partial rebound at close.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar stages partial rebound at close.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar staged a partial rebound on Friday after concerted selling pressure early in the session took it sharply lower.
By the close, Kiwi was at US$0.6945/52, having opened at 0.6965/72. The trade-weighted Index closed at 67.98 from 68.34.
Heavy offshore selling pressure early in the day took the currency down to $0.6950, where some buying emerged.
But another wave, which coincided with weakness in the Australian dollar, took it down to 0.6919, triggering stops along the way.
"It's not too surprising to see a modest bounce," said one dealer, noting a similar rebound in the Aussie.

"Interest rates really haven't gone up more than five or six points so that's quite comfortable - a better combination for (Reserve Bank Govnernor) Don Brash and (Treasurer) Winston Peters," said the dealer.
The market largely ignored comments from Labour Party Finance spokesman Michael cullen, who called for direct intervention in the market to tackle the high Kiwi.
"I think we could see it move back to that 0.6985-95 level over the next 36 hours or so, but I think you'll find plenty of fresh selling in the Kiwi at 0.6980 to 0.7010," he said.

"Longer term I think the jury is very much out on the Kiwi. This selling that has been coming through here, I don't think a lot of people expected it," he said. "At the moment I think we are at a bit of a crossroads," he said.
"It could test lower in the immediate future. Kiwi at some stage will become value for money again. It's not there yet," he said.
"I'm still cautiously bullish for the Kiwi but this correction could develop into something a bit deeper than people are giving it credit for."
